LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 10.3.1 WORD CLASSES: DETERMINERS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.3: Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we indicate that something belongs to somebody?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify articles and possessives in texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. articulate signs of articles and possessives in texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use articles and possessives in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the importance of articles and possessives for effective communication. ● In pairs, learners are guided to underline articles [a, an, the] and possessives [my, our, your, his, her, their] used in print and non-print texts. ● In pairs, learners are guided to fingerspell and sign articles and possessives articles [a, an, the] and possessives [my, our, your, his, her, their]. ● In pairs, learner is guided to sign read examples of possessives from flashcards. ● In pairs, learners are guided to correct errors in sentences that contain articles. ● In groups, learners are guided to engage in language games using articles. ● In pairs, learners are guided to practise matching articles with nouns. ● In pairs, learners are guided to construct signed sentences using possessives. ● Individually, learner is guided to construct written sentences using possessives. How do we indicate that something belongs to somebody? 99 ● In groups, learners are guided to compose a signed song on children’s rights using relevant articles and possessives and video record the performances.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: Learner develops self awareness skills as they pay attention to details and correct errors in sentences.

● Communication and collaboration: Learner develops speaking or signing skills as they use articles and possessives to communicate

clearly and effectively.

Values:
● Respect: Is nurtured as learners use articles and possessives ,which enables them to use correct titles while addressing people

Link to other Subjects

The learner relates the concepts of articles and possessives to their learning in other languages such as Kiswahili.

Suggested Learning Resources

Word cards, Class readers, Adapted Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g. tablets and mobile phones, Dictionary, Internet,

Signed audio-visual recordings, Posters, Pictures and Photographs ,Extracts from newspapers, magazines and books, E-books, Internet,

Online dictionaries, Digital story books, Projector, Computers, digital devices.

3. use articles and possessives in sentences,
